sources: Binding invariant comments in code (ordering contract on generated ids; comment far from the change)
Directory-scoped and root CLAUDE.md rule files (repository rules applied to code)
Python module-level side effects at import (network I/O executed on import)

defects.class: documented ordering constraint violated by reorder
defects.rule: # NOTE: ids are assigned in ascending order and consumers rely on it; do not reorder
defects.description: Input incoming=[LOT-B expiry 2027-03-01, LOT-A expiry 2026-11-30] (receipt order B then A). Before the change ids are LOT-B=101, LOT-A=102 in receipt order. After the change _prepare_batch sorts by expiry, so LOT-A=101 and LOT-B=102, and the returned list is reordered. The NOTE at line 26 forbids reordering; a consumer that pairs id 101 with the first received pallet (LOT-B) now receives LOT-A. The reorder call is at line 28.

defects.class: config key read without default in defaults file
defects.rule: New config keys must be added to config.defaults.toml with a default value.
defects.description: receiving.max_pallets_per_batch is read at line 35 but is absent from code/config.defaults.toml and no override is supplied. With default configuration, receive_batch(store, [one valid scan], [lot]) raises KeyError at the settings lookup before any pallet is validated, so every batch fails.

defects.rule: No network calls at import time: modules must not open sockets, send HTTP requests or read remote resources while being imported. Do the work inside functions called at runtime.
defects.description: LOGO_BYTES performs an HTTP request at import. Importing reports.cofa_template on an offline worker or in CI (no route to cdn.lab-assets.internal) raises URLError during import, so every module that imports the template module (report worker, tests) fails to load, and each import repeats the request.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: A TODO note about a future change. It is not a rule, has no runtime effect, and the current code it sits above is the one D1 covers; the comment itself is not a violation.
receiving.scan_timeout_s is added to both code/config.defaults.toml (scan_timeout_s = 30.0) and the code, so the rule is satisfied; the read happens inside fetch_supplier_asn at runtime.
urllib.request is imported at module level, but no request is made at import; the only urlopen call is inside fetch_supplier_asn, which runs when called.

Real flaw on an unchanged line: the mutable default totals={} is shared across calls, so summarise_by_material([A 10 g]) followed by summarise_by_material([B 5 g]) returns {A: 10, B: 5}. Not part of the change; a diff-mode reviewer must not report it.
